1

Details

Why cosmics now. The ILL feasibility study (x17_facility_search/ill/) found cosmics a substantial background there, with two handles: the arm-to-arm time of flight and collinearity. At n_TOF, sept26_prelim_analysis/tight_coincidence.py already vetoes opposing pairs above 170° (BACK_TO_BACK_DEG), 40 % of the tight opposing sample, but nothing used the timing direction, and the beam-off runs were cut at stage 0 and never read.

What exists so far. An inventory of all 47 beam-off runs (ntof_cosmics/inventory.py) and a clock match of DREAM cosmic triggers to n_TOF without beam (ntof_cosmics/clock_match.py), demonstrated on one 15-minute sub-run. Long-form reports: ntof_cosmics/results/report.html and results/clock_match/report.html.

A straight-through particle mimics a back-to-back pair; three handles separate it

Schematic top view, not to scale. A and C oppose; B and D are perpendicular.

One background, whatever its source. A single particle crossing the set-up in a straight line, cosmic or beam punch-through, is the same category for X17.

1 · Collinearity, opening angle ≈ 180°. In use already: back_to_back. The cosmic runs can set the cut from data.

2 · Capsule vertex: through-goers pass the capsule only as often as the acceptance allows; real pairs come from it.

3 · Time-of-flight sign: a ~2–3 ns lag, below the ~7 ns Δt resolution per event, but visible as a shift on the >170° sample. Needs the clock match in this note.

Hover the dotted terms and chart points for definitions and numbers.

2

Details

The framing (Dylan, 2026-10-02): it does not matter whether a through-going track is a cosmic or beam background. If a single particle crosses from one side to the other in a straight line, it is one category, and the beam-off runs are the clean, high-statistics sample of that topology. They give its signature and the efficiency of any veto, not a separate background to subtract.

Handle 2 should use pointing estimators (the closest approach of the line to the capsule), not the shape of a position distribution: CLAUDE.md, "Take positions from pointing".

Handle 3 needs scintillator times for cosmic events, which only n_TOF records. Hence the rest of this note.

3

Details

Source: ntof_cosmics/inventory.py → results/cosmic_runs.csv (47 rows) and cosmic_subruns.csv (273). Inputs, none typed by hand: the frozen EOS survey (dylan-cern-site/data/x17-runs.json), each run's run_config.json, the per-minute beam_class slow-control log (n_TOF-destined pulses only), the match ledger and the n_TOF completed ledger.

The cosmic runs were substituted automatically whenever the beam dropped, which is why they are many and short, and why beam appears at their edges. The beam flag has one-minute resolution: a sub-run shorter than ~6 min has almost no "interior", so run_157 (0.031 Hz residual beam across 7 minutes) is classed "edges". Any analysis must veto by pulse time, not by this flag.

Conditions: everything at the production point is after the 23-July noise change. run_80 still has chamber A x connector 8 dead (live from run_83). run_148 is empty. PLAN §S4 had named run_83 and run_146 for the cosmic rate: 0.6 h between them. run_149 alone is 21.8 h.

n_TOF kept recording with no beam for 15 h, and catches ~16 % of the cosmic triggers

Top: how the two DAQs overlap. Bottom right: where n_TOF was recording, per cosmic run.

With no protons, n_TOF free-runs: an 80 ms window every 0.5009 s, a 16 % duty cycle. PKUP still stamps every window with a psTime.

So about 16 % of DREAM's 25 Hz cosmic triggers fall inside a window, and n_TOF records the same particle in its walls and plastics: the only place a cosmic gets a scintillator time.

4

Details

n_TOF's own run log does not say "random trigger"; it shows as runs whose bunches carry no beam: PulseIntensity = 0, user and lsaCycle = −1, and ~50 kB per bunch against ~10 MB with beam. inventory.py classes an n_TOF run as recording-without-protons below 0.5 MB/bunch, a gap of two decades. Runs 224678–687 (with run_149) and 224608–613 (with run_103) are the bulk.

The window length is read from the data: the largest wall tof in 224678 is 79.999 ms. The period is the spacing of consecutive psTime values, 0.50077–0.50099 s.

340 of 4514 bunches of 224678 have psTime = 0 and are dropped for now; the period is regular enough to recover them from their neighbours.

5

Details

DREAM. Absolute time = the go instant + timestamp × 10 ns, from FEU 1's decoded_root (not combined_hits, which keeps only events with Micromegas activity). Go is not logged; the DAQ log's "Subrun started" line (PC clock, ms) is the anchor and S absorbs the difference.

n_TOF. Absolute time = psTime of the bunch + δ_b + tof. The stored tflash is meaningless without beam and is not used, which has a side effect: raw tof has no common zero across detector trees (next-to-last slide).

The beam-on map (ntof_dream_merge/DREAM_NTOF_CALIBRATION.md) is t_nTOF = t_DREAM(1 + K) + T0 + a_arm + δa_b + δk_b·t, in time since the flash. Here the flash is replaced by psTime, and δa_b (6.5 ns RMS with beam) becomes δ_b (tens of µs).

t_DREAM_on_nTOF = t_log + S + td·(1 + k)
off             = t_DREAM_on_nTOF − psTime_b = δ_b + tof·(1 − κ)

One translation stands out of ±60 s: S = +6.450 s, where beam-on runs predict

First 60 s of run_149 cos_0000: every n_TOF singles minus every DREAM trigger.

6

Details

1563 DREAM triggers against every singles candidate within ±60 s: the flat floor is the 0.5 s n_TOF comb against uncorrelated triggers; the slow shape is the overlap of the slice with the run's span. The peak survives a zoom from 1 ms to 10 µs to 100 ns bins before the rate starts to smear it.

The prior. On beam sub-runs DREAM's start is known from the pulse lock: file-name minute + pulse_match offset − log line − 0.829 s (the NXCALS publication lag) puts go on the psTime clock. 14 sub-runs give 5.5–13.4 s; 7 land at −100 s or +21–24 s, which are supercycle mislocks in a cache that predates the lock fix (ntof_processing/join_mislock/). Grey dots on the strip.

Sources: results/clock_match/beam_on_log_starts.txt, ntof_july_analysis/cache_pulse_match/.

The drift is 3.8 ppm, not the in-window 110 ppm: a line carries S across the sub-run

Every pair within ±5 ms of the coarse translation, all 900 s.

With S fixed, a ±5 ms window around every trigger follows a straight line: DREAM runs 3.8 ppm fast against psTime, 3.5 ms over the 15-minute sub-run.

run_149 cosbounce_cos_0000 ↔ n_TOF 224678 · grey: every (DREAM trigger, singles) pair within ±5 ms.

7

Details

The windows shrink in three steps (5 ms, 1 ms, 200 µs); at each the robust line (3σ clipping, four passes) is refitted on the pairs inside it. The fit converges by the second step.

Two rates, not one: between bunches DREAM drifts -3.84 ppm against psTime; inside a window it runs 117 ppm against the n_TOF digitiser (κ, next slide). The beam-on calibration only ever saw the second, because with beam each burst is re-locked to its own flash.

The line is not the whole story: the per-bunch offsets (slide 9) show a slow wander of ~277 µs, the curvature a straight line misses. A smooth drift model is on the list.

Inside a window the clocks differ by κ = 116.6 ppm, within 6 ppm of beam-on

Bunches holding exactly two matched triggers: their difference against their tof separation.

Two triggers in the same bunch share δ_b and psTime, so their difference sees only the in-window rate: 376 such bunches give κ = 116.6 ppm.

About them, the pair difference has σ = 15 ns, i.e. ~11 ns per trigger.

The mild growth with separation is the per-bunch rate jitter (~1 ppm with beam), not yet fitted.

8

Details

off − tof for a real pair is δ_b − κ·tof. Taking the difference of the two triggers of one bunch removes δ_b, and the slope against their tof separation is −κ. Robust line, 3σ clipping; red points are the clipped ones (accidental partners).

The beam-on calibration notes that K is per (DREAM run, n_TOF processing) pair and must be re-fitted, not transported; a +6.2 ppm difference between run_79 ↔ 224572 and run_149 ↔ 224678 is consistent with that. At 80 ms it is a 497 ns effect, so transporting K would have cost resolution at late tof.

Each free-running window starts ~30 µs off its psTime, at random, on a slow wander

Per-bunch window offset from the bunch's matched triggers (median), run_149 cos_0000 ↔ 224678.

Without beam, nothing pins where each 80 ms window starts. Measured per bunch from its own triggers, δ_b has two parts:

slow: a wander of 277 µs over the sub-run, the curvature the straight drift line misses. It can be followed.

fast: 29 µs MAD, uncorrelated bunch to bunch (neighbour step 43 µs ≈ √2 × it). It cannot.

So a trigger alone in its bunch (418 here) is placed only to ~30 µs. Two or more, and δ_b is measured.

9

Details

δ_b = median over the bunch's matched triggers of off − tof·(1 − κ), where off is the DREAM trigger time on the drift map minus psTime. 1328 bunches carry at least one matched trigger.

With beam the equivalent per-burst offset δa_b is 6.5 ns RMS, because every burst re-locks to its gamma flash. Here the window start is tied to psTime only through whatever free-running trigger n_TOF used, and the scatter is ~5000× larger. It is a property of n_TOF's beam-off acquisition, not of DREAM.

Not yet tried: a smooth (spline) drift model in stage 2 would absorb the slow part and let the stage-4 association window shrink from ±300 µs.

10

Details

Efficiency, honestly counted. Numerator: triggers whose leave-one-out residual is within ±50 ns. Denominator: every DREAM trigger that falls, on the drift map, inside a bunch window (100 µs clear of either edge) whose δ_b is known from other triggers, whether or not it found a candidate. The first version of this number counted only triggers that already had a candidate within 300 µs, which inflated it to 92.9 %.

Compared with beam-on. The beam-on match (run_79 ↔ 224572) reaches 96.0 % (wall AND plastic) with a 6 ns 68 % half-width. The ~4-point gap here is not yet understood; candidates are the unfitted per-bunch rate and the 418 single-trigger bunches, which leave the denominator but could bias which bunches enter it.

Accidentals. The nearest-candidate residual 1–300 µs from the peak is accidental by construction; scaled to ±50 ns it predicts 0.0002. Analytically: 27 Hz of in-window singles × 100 ns × 2664 triggers ≈ 0.007.

Four things that would have silently broken the match

Each found on the way and handled in clock_match.py.

combined_hits ≠ every trigger

It keeps only events with Micromegas activity. The clock match reads FEU 1's decoded_root timestamp (10 ns ticks): all 22 760 triggers.

psTime = 0 on 7.5 % of bunches

340 of 4514 in 224678. Dropped for now; the 0.5009 s period is regular to ~0.1 ms, so they are recoverable.

Raw tof has no common zero

With beam, each tree's own tflash absorbs its cable delay. Without, the plastics sit 35–42 ns late, outside the 20 ns coincidence: 0 singles until shifted.

PSSA

39.1 ns

34.4 ns

41.7 ns

40.8 ns

The cached lock has mislocks

7 of 21 beam-on pulse-match offsets in the local cache are supercycle steps off. Fine as a prior here; never as a constant.

11

Details

The plastic shift is measured in situ per arm (clock_match.measure_pss_shift): the peak of plastic − wall-sum times within ±2 µs, median within ±30 ns, then moved to the beam-on peak (A −6.8, B −3.8, C −6.3, D −8.8 ns, DREAM_NTOF_CALIBRATION.md §2b) so the emulated AND sees the timing the hardware did.

fast_singles is reused unchanged; only its reader is swapped (_raw_tof_reader) to hand it raw tof instead of tof − tflash.

What this does not rule out

One sub-run

run_149 cos_0000 ↔ 224678 only. S is per sub-run; k and κ should transfer but are not yet shown to.

Single-trigger bunches

418 triggers alone in their window are placed only to ~30 µs, and leave the denominator.

A straight drift line

The slow δ_b wander is curvature it misses; a smooth model would tighten stage 4.

92 % against 96 %

The gap to the beam-on efficiency is not yet understood.

No tracking yet

Nothing here says how many cosmic triggers carry a track, or a track in two arms.
